task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: how to define shaper and distinguish cut-heavy vs drive-heavy
how to measure role travel (portability) after a team move
sample size sufficiency with n=24 units
confounding by team context and landing-spot quality
reliability of play-type classification for cut and drive
potential endogeneity of pre-move role assignment

historical_evidence.finding: Pre-move cut share (vs drive share) predicted whether a connector's organizational function reproduced after a move: cut share rho=+0.265 p=0.011 AUC 0.653; cut-drive rho=+0.314 p=0.002; drive rho=-0.278 p=0.007. Top cut tercile 65% portable median Delta +0.167; bottom 35% median -0.039. LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005. n=92 connector movers.

Binary match rate 15.7%. Connector delta match vs mismatch med +0.540 vs +0.069 p=0.156 n=5/14. Travel-check delta p=0.413. All-movers delta p=0.0283 but Spearman(match_score, delta)=-0.034 p=0, not replicated as continuous and not the licensed connector test. n=19 taxonomy connectors, 198 all movers.
Observed gap -0.066 PPP below MDE 0.180; n=44 cannot distinguish true null from effect up to 0.18 PPP. MDE 0.180 at 80% power (SD~0.34).
Stated underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality; no numbers reported. Dropped from Paper 1.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Diet-matching to destination structural-gap for connector movers
failed_approaches.why: Question untestable: connector subset n=19/40, extreme small sample; binary match rate low; continuous Spearman null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing DRIVE as BEST counter vs constrained baseline
failed_approaches.why: Low power, large MDE: n=44, MDE 0.18 PPP at 80% power, observed gap below MDE.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Destination net rating checks for movers
failed_approaches.why: Underpowered, null after correction; dropped from paper.

evidence_establishes: Cut-heavy connectors' organizational function is more portable across team moves than drive-heavy connectors, as shown by positive Spearman correlations, tercile hit rates, and permutation tests (n=92).
Drive-heavy connectors tend to have worse portability (negative correlation).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the effect holds specifically for the 'shaper' role (low-usage, positive residual structural influence) rather than the broader 'connector' category used in prior work.
Whether the effect can be detected with only n=24 shaper movers, given prior small-sample limitations.
Causal mechanisms or confounding by coaching, roster context, or definitional overlap between shaper and connector.
own_inferences: The shaper role is a subset of players likely to overlap with connectors, but the exact overlap is unknown from the retrieved records; the prior result may partially generalise.
n=24 units is far below the 92 used in the positive study and is almost certainly underpowered for any effect similar to r≈0.27; an MDE would be large and likely impractical.
Even if the question is not exactly answered, a study with n=24 would likely be untestable or produce an inconclusive result.
uncertainties: Distribution of pre-move cut share among shapers: if shapers are uniformly cut-heavy, variation may be insufficient.
Potential confounders like team system changes, coaching changes, and player role re-definition after a move.
Stability of the shaper classification across seasons and teams.

historical_effect.explanation: The prior positive result ([prior work]) increases confidence that the underlying relationship exists, but the critical constraint is n=24 shaper movers, which is insufficient for adequate power regardless of the prior evidence. The decision remains do_not_proceed due to sample size.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 24 shaper movers available; prior study needed 92 connectors to detect r≈0.27. Power for this design would be too low to distinguish a true effect from null, MDE likely >0.4 in correlation terms.
If most shapers cluster on one side of the cut-drive spectrum, the predictor variance will be small, making a comparison between cut-heavy and drive-heavy subgroups unreliable.
Team system, coach, and role assignment changes may confound post-move portability, and with n=24, covariate adjustment is limited.

prior_work.summary: Prior work already tested and supported the hypothesis that cut share predicts connector portability (n=92). The present question narrows the population to shapers and constrains to n=24, which introduces sample-size problems.

risks.text: n=24 is severely underpowered; the prior positive result required n=92 for a modest effect size. The minimal detectable effect would be large, and the study risks returning an inconclusive null even if an effect exists.
Cut-heavy vs drive-heavy may be an imbalanced split among shapers, reducing effective comparison size.
Post-move role portability may be influenced by coaching, team play-style, or player ageing, not just pre-move cut/drive tendencies.

The shaper classification is derived from structural influence, which is itself sensitive to team context and could change purely due to roster composition, creating circularity with portability measures.
Reliability of play-type labels (cut vs drive) from the inferrer may vary across teams, affecting predictor measurement.
Implicitly looking at many player-role subgroups increases false-positive risk; the prior connector result may not be independent.

design.estimand: Difference in role portability (post-move structural influence or play-type mix continuity) between shapers in the top tercile of pre-move cut share versus the bottom tercile, adjusting for destination team quality.
design.unit: Shaper mover (a player classified as a Shaper in the season before a team move, with a minimum of N games played).
design.sample: All shaper movers identified across NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons; currently n=24. Minimum viable sample would require at least 80 shaper movers (based on prior effect size r=0.27, 80% power, one-sided Spearman).
design.power: With n=24, power is below 30% for r=0.27; MDE for 80% power exceeds r=0.50. The study is not adequately powered unless the true effect is implausibly large.
design.controls: Age, change in team quality (net rating), coach change (indicator), games missed in transition, pre-move usage, destination shaper competition.
design.falsification: Permutation test with 5000 label shuffles of cut-share tercile, and a placebo test using non-mover shapers randomly assigned a fictional 'move' date.
design.multiplicity: Single primary hypothesis (cut-heavy vs drive-heavy); exploratory: continuous cut share and cut-minus-drive share.
design.decision_rule: Reject null of no difference if Spearman rho (cut share vs portability delta) is positive with one-sided p < 0.025 after permutation correction, with pre-registered dropping of extreme outliers.
design.data_version: NBA play-by-play and derived play-type initiations from 2022-23 through 2025-26 as of 2026-08-08.
